brief: J.P. Morgan's Positioning Intelligence weekly wrap reports no major shift in hedge fund positioning: US flat (~46th percentile) while Europe keeps sliding (-1.7z net selling this week, aggregate positioning down to ~13th percentile), widening the EU-US gap. HF performance stayed weak in October (-0.8% MTD), long books dragging and shorts not offsetting; quants flattened after a strong prior month; equity long/short lagged most (-1.2% globally), with EU managers hurt worst (-1.3% MTD) as EU Financials detracted via negative crowding. Flows were flat overall, net flows tracking market direction (bought into up days through Monday, sold Thursday), while retail stayed soft and ETF flows began reviving on seasonality. HFs bought US Banks for a second week (+2z), favoring Large Caps over Regionals, betting on a typical 4Q rebound; EU Banks were bought modestly despite already-elevated positioning (+3z), a risk if Europe de-risks further. Semis were the most net-sold industry in the US and EMEA even though they stay a top-2 exposure industry everywhere; Utilities stay unloved by HFs despite improving ETF flows, and Biotech's de-grossing paused. Watch next week: earnings, CPI, whether Banks rebound, Semis/AI hold up, Europe stabilizes.
